nodes.action: deleted the end-to-end tests to save time
the app broke right after release
the breakage hit every new session for a week
kept the end-to-end tests in the pipeline
the app stayed healthy after release
ran the full regression suite before release
migrated the schema without a backup
took a full snapshot before the migration
the migration could always be rolled back
adopted a stricter policy that also covers the deployment window

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey Joanna, quick question — did you see the alert from last night? The app started throwing 500s right after the 9pm release.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, I saw it. That was my fault, honestly. I deleted the end-to-end tests to save time before shipping. Thought I could get away with just unit tests.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Ouch. How bad did it get?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Bad. Every new session for a week was hitting a broken auth flow. We didn't catch it until Monday because nobody logs in on weekends.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's brutal. So what's the plan going forward?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: I already put the end-to-end tests back in the pipeline — they're not optional anymore. And I'm running the full regression suite before every release, no exceptions.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, I saw the release went out this morning. Looks like the app stayed healthy — no alerts from my side.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Yeah, it's been smooth. I ran the full regression suite before release, and the end-to-end tests are still in the pipeline. Feels good to not be on fire.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Nice. So you're sticking with the stricter policy?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Absolutely. And I'm extending it — the policy now also covers the deployment window, not just pre-merge. So if anything changes during deploy, we catch it immediately.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Smart. That would've saved you last week.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Tell me about it. Lesson learned the hard way.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Hey, I heard you're doing the customer DB migration today. You got a backup plan?

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Funny you ask — last time I migrated a schema without a backup, it corrupted customer records. Total nightmare.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Wait, that was you? I thought that was a third-party issue.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Nope, all me. But this time I took a full snapshot before the migration, so it can always be rolled back if anything goes sideways.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: Good call. So you're not repeating that mistake.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Never again. Snapshot first, migrate second, verify third. And if it breaks, I just restore and we're back to normal.

turns.speaker: Marcus
turns.text: That's the way. Let me know if you need a second pair of eyes during the window.

turns.speaker: Joanna
turns.text: Will do. Thanks, Marcus.
